newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse announces plan to split in two.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse announces plan to split in two.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp, as expected, announced plans to focus on its broadcast assets by splitting in two and spinning off its industrial business in a tax-free distribution to shareholders.
The company said the $4.6 billion spinoff would create a new Pittsburgh-based company to be called Westinghouse Electric Co, or WELCO for short.
Westinghouse also plans to offer up to 20 percent of its Thermo King unit in a public stock offering.
Westinghouse is taking a one-time charge of $125 million in the 1996 fourth quarter to cover severance and related costs. The company plans to eliminate 1,100 jobs as part of its restructuring.
Westinghouse's separate broadcast company, to be headquartered in New York, will have its own board of directors and be headed by current Westinghouse Chairman Michael Jordan.
A new chief executive officer will be named for WELCO prior to the spinoff.

After the spinoff, Westinghouse Electric Corp (the current parent company) will consist of the CBS Inc television network, Group W Satellite Communications Co, a cable television marketing and distribution company, and Infinity Broadcasting, which Westinghouse is acquiring.

Westinghouse said it is divesting its Security Systems businesses and restructuring its Pittsburgh corporate headquarters and other industrial businesses to significantly cut WELCO's overhead and operating costs.

The separation of the two companies is expected to take nine months and is subject to a ruling from the Internal Revenue Service that the transaction will not be taxable to Westinghouse shareholders or to Westinghouse.
Westinghouse said it had opted for the plan because its board expects it will maximize the long-term after-tax value for shareholders.
The broadcast company will retain all debt obligations of the current Westinghouse Electric Corp as well as the company's $1.8 billion tax net operating loss carryforward.
WELCO will assume most of the unfunded pension obligations and other non-debt obligations generated in the past by Westinghouse's industrial companies.

WELCO will receive the proceeds of the Thermo King public offering as initial cash funding. WELCO's four business units will be Thermo King, Power Generation, Energy Systems and Government Operations.
The restructuring includes consolidating staffs of its corporate and industrial group headquarters as well as a number of administrative functions in the business units.
Several operations and processes in the Energy Systems business have been re-engineered to improve productivity and address changing market conditions in the power industry, Westinghouse said.
